Definition: The probability of a threat exploiting a vulnerability, combined with the resulting business impact.
Determining risk using hard financial data and historical statistics to estimate dollar amounts.
Determining risk using subjective judgment, experience, and descriptive labels such as Low, Medium, and High.
Single Loss Expectancy -- the financial cost of a single occurrence of a threat, often calculated as Asset Value times Exposure Factor.
Annualized Rate of Occurrence -- the estimated number of times a threat will occur in a year (0.1 means once in ten years).
Annualized Loss Expectancy -- the total financial loss expected from a threat per year, calculated as SLE times ARO.
Appetite is the broad willingness to take risk for strategic goals; tolerance is the specific, measurable limit around that appetite.
The four choices for facing risk: Mitigation (reducing), Transference (insurance), Avoidance (canceling), or Acceptance (a knowing, documented decision to live with it).
Governance, Risk, and Compliance platforms used to map controls, automate audits, and provide continuous security monitoring.
Advanced Persistent Threat -- a highly funded, government-sponsored (nation-state) adversary focused on espionage or destructive cyber warfare.
An adversary primarily motivated by ideology or politics rather than financial gain.
Adversaries motivated purely by financial gain, often operating Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) operations.
An adversary, malicious or accidental, who already has legitimate access to the internal network.
The risk that a third-party vendor (or the vendor's vendor) suffers a breach that exposes the primary organization's data.
An attack that targets a software flaw the vendor does not yet know about, so no patch exists.
A framework modeling the seven sequential phases of a cyberattack, from reconnaissance to actions on objectives.
A granular knowledge base of real-world adversary tactics and techniques.
A software threat-modeling framework covering Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, and Elevation of Privilege.
A catalog of common attack patterns (CAPEC) and the OWASP Top 10 list of the most critical web application security risks.
The total sum of all possible points where an unauthorized user can enter or extract data from an environment.
Any point in a system where data changes its level of trust, such as passing from the public internet into a private network.
Connected backups are fast but vulnerable to ransomware; disconnected (air-gapped) backups are offline and out of reach of network-based attacks.
Transmitting database transaction logs offsite in real time to prevent data loss.
The risk that remains after treatment; it must fall within the organization's risk tolerance.
An intrusion-analysis model linking adversary, capability, infrastructure, and victim so analysts can pivot from known features to unknown ones.

The Business Impact Analysis identifies critical functions; the Recovery Time Objective is the longest acceptable outage; the Recovery Point Objective is the most data loss acceptable, measured in time.
The risk that personal data is handled in ways that violate law or individuals' expectations, including data subject rights, data sovereignty, and biometric data.
